title: Quicksplice handoff notes — 03/13 night shift
content:
Context:
Quick, messy notes for the overnight handoff. This was a mid-load regression where a recent caching change (kv-cache sticky heuristics) produced a high miss rate and caused 502/503 spikes for text-gen endpoints with long-context models. I applied a temporary mitigation (route to small-model pool + disable sticky prefix caching) and we're currently stable but with higher cost and slightly increased latency.

Why this doc exists (notes-to-self):
- capture exact steps I ran so daytime SREs/product can reproduce/clean up
- list open questions for the engineering owner (Marco)
- record temporary config values and why we left them that way

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- 00:45 UTC: Increased 502 errors for /v1/generate on region-us-east-1 (p50 -> 220ms, p95 -> 3.6s, error rate ~4.2%)
- 01:08 UTC: Identified kv-cache miss surge on model: rdx-claidev-13b (sticky prefix hit rate dropped from ~0.78 to ~0.12)
- 01:20 UTC: Mitigation applied: route traffic to rdx-claidev-6b pool for lower-latency fallback; toggled FEATURE_KV_STICKY=false in runtime feature flags for affected pool
- 01:30 UTC: Error rate dropped to ~0.2%; latency stabilized p95 ~1.5s; cost increased ~12% due to fallback + smaller model inefficiency

What I did (commands + links):
- checked dashboards: Console -> per-route metrics -> /v1/generate -> filter region=us-east-1
- logs: kubectl -n inference logs -l svc=runtime-gateway --since=2h | grep "502" | head -n 50
- investigated cache stats: curl -s "http://metrics-host:9100/kv-cache/stats?model=rdx-claidev-13b" | jq
- feature flag toggle (temporary): POST https://config-api.internal/flags/FEATURE_KV_STICKY/pools/rdx-claidev-13b -> {"value": false} (done via admin UI at https://config.internal/flags)
- routing rule: created a canary routing rule to send 30% traffic to rdx-claidev-6b pool: GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/489 (deployed to staging then prod via rollout)

Observed metrics after mitigation: (approx)
- error rate -> 0.18%
- kv-cache hit rate (13b pool) -> still low (~0.15) because clients had warmed inconsistent prefixes
- cost delta -> +12% hourly for that region (estimate from billing-aggregates)

Open/root causes (hypotheses):
- the new sticky heuristics (prefix fingerprinting) regressed for long multi-turn sessions — it overbroke cache keys so the KV cache got scatter-saturated
- a client produced many slightly different prompts due to ephemeral metadata in the prefix (timestamp/user-id) causing near-unique keys
- kernel selection change around 02/10 improved token throughput but inhibited fallback behavior under high miss rates

Immediate follow-ups (who/what):
- Marco A (eng-serv): investigate PR #489 side-effects on prefix fingerprinting; reproduce locally with long multi-turn traces (assigned JIRA-3581)
- Priya S (runtime): audit clients for metadata in prompt prefix (we suspect an SDK wrapper added ephemeral device-id)
- Lina (me): leave the routing / flag state as-is unless error rate >0.5% for next 6 hours; collect heap/eviction traces at 03:00 UTC and attach to JIRA

Temporary config values (please revert once root-cause fix is merged and validated):
- FEATURE_KV_STICKY=false (pool: rdx-claidev-13b)
- Routing: /v1/generate region-us-east-1: 70% -> rdx-claidev-13b (sticky off), 30% -> rdx-claidev-6b
- Autoscale min-replicas bumped from 2 -> 3 for rdx-claidev-6b (to handle sudden shift)

Manual rollback steps (if things worsen):
1) Re-enable sticky flag: POST to config-api -> {"value": true} (note: re-enable only after PR fix)
2) Revert routing rule via console: delete canary rule or set traffic split back to 100% 13b pool
3) Scale-down rdx-claidev-6b min-replicas back to 2 to conserve cost
4) Notify #sre-alerts and create incident note in JIRA-3581 with timestamps/metrics

Short checklist for whoever takes next shift:
- [ ] Check /v1/generate error rate and p95 latency for us-east-1 at top of shift
- [ ] Confirm kv-cache hit/miss rates for 13b pool (metrics endpoint above)
- [ ] If error rate >0.5%: escalate to on-call eng (pager) and follow manual rollback steps
- [ ] Add the 00:45-01:30 traces to JIRA-3581 (location: /artifacts/traces/quicksplice/2026-03-13)
- [ ] If stable for 6h, coordinate with Marco to revert FEATURE_KV_STICKY and run canary tests

Misc notes / things I scribbled while debugging:
- saw a weird client pattern: repeated `user_metadata: session_ts` values differ per token -> likely cause of unique cache keys
- small optimization idea: implement prefix-normalization hook in SDK to strip ephemeral fields before sending to runtime
- ensure we have a synthetic test that simulates long-turn sessions with minor prefix diffs (file: tests/synthetic/longturn-prefix-fuzz.sh)

Questions for daytime crew / product:
- Is it acceptable to keep the sticky heuristic off temporarily per compliance/cost? Product might push back on quality regression for some customers using 13b.
- Which customers should we proactively notify if we plan to route them to 6b for a sustained window? I flagged two high-traffic tenants in the guardrail list — need CS to confirm.

Contact/where to find me tonight:
- Slack: @lina.chen (available until 04:30 UTC)
- Phone: +1-415-555-0132 (use only for P1)

End notes:
- Saving this as a scratch handoff; will convert to formal incident postmortem if root cause confirmed.
- If you take over, add a short paragraph at the top summarizing any changes you made so daytime team doesn't re-run same toggles.

-- Lina
